direction: Strengthen the dimensionless capacity-fill reward and endpoint-demand-balance term in the globally depot-scale-normalized generalized savings score (lam~1.05, mu~0.12, beta~0.15-0.30 plus 1-|q_i-q_j|/(q_i+q_j) balance), keeping normalization fixed at mean(d[0,1:]), so that merge ordering packs tight-capacity and clustered instances into fewer fragmented routes before relocate_2opt polishing.

operations.mechanism: KB entry method-cvrp-m2-l2a-generalized-savings confirms the globally depot-mean-normalized score is the only safe normalization (per-pair normalization is an explicit antipattern that degrades dev_24 to ~16.7-18.1), and its open question section flags relocate_2opt combination plus stronger fill/balance weighting as untested residual-gain directions. Archive feedback shows the frontier is saturated between two variants of the same static merge (SBS 16.0067, VBS 16.0127 -> only 0.25% headroom), so the productive move is not a skeleton switch but evolutionary pressure on the capacity/balance coefficients, which directly targets the tight-capacity and clustered weak regimes; relocate_2opt postprocess is retained to convert the reduced route count into local distance gains while remaining well inside the 500 ms budget (~1% of it).

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Because the weakest dev_24 regimes are capacity_level=tight (vbs_rel_gap -22.2%) and spatial=clustered (-19.8%), residual error is dominated by tail-route fragmentation rather than bad long-edge ordering; therefore increasing the capacity-fill/balance reward (beta in [0.15,0.30] with demand-equilibrium term) while retaining the global depot-mean distance normalization will reduce mean objective below the current SBS 16.0067 on tight-capacity and clustered instances without degrading solve_ms beyond the ~3.6 ms already observed, since the hook stays a single vectorized scoring pass.
